findings.what: Creation's Dispositions text says 'None of them makes you better or worse at anything', but two sliders set starting abilities read by evaluation
findings.evidence: Conscientiousness sets Discipline = 30 + 0.5*c (5 -> 32.5, 95 -> 77.5), which lifts practice (attributes.ts:263) and feeds consistency in every task. Emotional Stability sets Composure = 25 + 0.35*s. The page lists neither effect.
findings.suggestedFix: Say on the page that Conscientiousness sets your starting Discipline and Emotional Stability your starting Composure, and drop the 'None of them makes you better' sentence. The other option is to decouple the abilities from the sliders, but that is the owner's call.

findings.what: The 'receipts' knob (Chaotic 0.9, Keeps Accounts 1.3) changes nothing in play
findings.evidence: recordJobCost is the only writer of y.jobCosts and has no production caller (it appears only in tests/costs.test.ts:54 and tests/arrears.test.ts:107), so the multiplier always applies to 0. Five places still claim the effect: the creation text (CharacterCreation.tsx:655-657), the trait descriptions and costs (personality-traits.ts:177,265), KNOB_READS.receipts, the trait look, and docs/UNBITTEN.md:193-198.
findings.suggestedFix: Either wire a real job-cost source, or log this in docs/UNBITTEN.md and make the text say it in the past tense. The second option also means taking 'receipts' off Chaotic and Keeps Accounts, or marking it in the trait look as not read now.

findings.what: The Home decision's 'Apply For OPT' button quietly adds premium processing
findings.evidence: The action payload is { premium: true }, which adds premiumFee 1,780 USD (content/workrules.ts:40). Papers offers 'Apply For OPT' (standard) and 'Apply With Premium Processing' as two separate buttons (src/ui/papers/Documents.tsx:196-197). No test covers this decision.
findings.suggestedFix: Label the button 'Apply For OPT, Premium Processing', or offer both. Add a test.

findings.what: Decision buttons get around the guide's command locks
findings.evidence: Only top-level commands are guarded. world.take_decision_action opens in the 'needs' chapter (content/tutorial.ts:99) and runs tax.file, bank.reactivate or documents.apply_opt nested, even while their chapters (tutorial.ts:215,229,265) are still locked.

findings.what: Home's Papers line understates tax owed and how fast it grows
findings.evidence: Home sums the stored r.owed (as of the last accrual), while PapersWorkspace.tsx:153 uses owedOn(r, now). Home says 'growing half a percent a month', but the engine also adds 7% a year interest (taxreturn.ts:69-100). Papers states both.
findings.suggestedFix: Use owedOn(r, sim.now) and say 'interest and a late-payment penalty'.

findings.what: The Profile's genre suggestion mislabels its fallback
findings.evidence: When there is no casting play, nextGenre returns the least-known loved genre, but the sentence still says it 'is the kind your next work asks for'.
findings.suggestedFix: Make nextGenre return its reason (play or loved) and word the sentence by it.

findings.what: Traits on the Player Profile can't be opened, and dispositions appear nowhere after creation
findings.evidence: Creation says 'Once you're playing, each opens from your own page into what it moves', but the Profile prints plain names. The trait look can only be reached from the person look (looks/wellbeing.tsx:117-120).
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap each trait in <Open subject={at('trait', id)}>. Consider showing the seven dispositions as well.

findings.what: Height and weight are dropped without a word when out of range or half filled
